cases.name: Debra Jean Helgerson
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Debra worked as an accounting specialist at Goodwill of West Texas since 2014, and part time for Terry Browder Sayles Ranch Guesthouses. Prior to that she worked at PepsiTexas for 19 years and part-time at Dillard's for 8 years. Deb was the ultimate fashionista and loved accessorizing as evidenced by her large collection of watches, shoes, and purses. Everything had to match head to toe. She loved finding a bargain. Her sense of humor was top notch and she could turn anything into a joke. She was a devoted mother to her daughter Tina. She was also an avid Green Bay Packer fan but couldn't watch the games because she would get too anxious. She loved being with her family."

She also received a Bachelor of Political Science / Pre-Law with a minor in Counseling and Human Development degree from Hardin-Simmons and she also received her Masters from Hardin-Simmons. She was a faithful member of Oak Grove Baptist Church and sung in the choir. She is best known for her peaceful and beautiful loving spiritual character. Humility was a natural gift of hers. Judi was a loving and caring mother. She spent her life supporting her children in every possible way for them to succeed in life."

cases.name: Unnamed Infant Girl
cases.narrative:
He admitted to being “too aggressive” when he was trying to get her to stop crying. He admitted when she started crying, he forced her facedown onto the couch and covered her with a pillow while he spanked her, in an attempt to “muffle her screams”. He admitted to putting the pillow over her head 5-6 times and also squeezed her sides and grabbed the back of her head.

Autopsy results showed signs of abuse, including “skull fractures caused by blunt force trauma, a large contusion on the head caused by multiple blunt force impacts, and broken ribs that were not consistent with CPR.”
